podcast.body: Prince demoed this song in 1984, and it was later recorded once by his funk band, The Family, in 1985. However, it did not gain traction until Sinead O'Connor's manager suggested it to her, leading to her massively successful version. Prince was reportedly unhappy with Sinead's version due to her "foul language" in interviews, leading to "serious friction" when they met. "Steve thought the song might be perfect for Shanade. He took the song into the studio with engineer Chris Berket, who'd also mixed a couple of songs from her first album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Prince's heartbreak ballad, famously covered by Sinéad O'Connor in 1990, whose rendition became a number one hit. "Prince's Heartbreak Ballad, Nothing Comparious To You."
